name: Aarav's Determintion
story: One day my kid was really unwell. He had fever and vomitted twice in front of me. Inspite of me and other volunteers repeatedly telling him to go rest, he didn't go. He was sitting there with me, trying to learn. He said he doesn't want to go but wants to study. That moment filled my heart with joy and pride. During the earlier classes, he usually didn't want to sit and learn and would always ask "Miss, class over? Can I go?". But seeing him sit in class even though being sick was a miracle. We managed to instill the desire to study in him🥹

name: Shreyas and the 3 magical words
story:
This moment happened just recently. When I never expected it will happen.( So in real you don't expect what will happen when though😅). But yes, I have regularly taught my kids English and they have learnt a lot from. Whether it be playing word games, playing subjective action games, my ace game scrabble with word blocks and what not.....
I usually teach them in a very fun and sweet-strict way.Our centre usually holds one of the highest number of kids who are really enthusiastic and run all around the place. So to call them down we actually need to hold the T symbol number of times.
But the story is not related to this though.
Ok where were we.. yes I usually teach many kids on different days, but my kids usually be there with me every class.
One incident is where we had a behavioral-manners drama. And my kid literally asked the other kid " Please pass the eraser". The cherry on the cake was some totally other kid came to me and asked " Anna what do I say if I need to ask for colours".
Back to my kids, we had an activity of vision boards where we had to make the kids motivations and inspiration. One's fav was Jasprit Bumrah and the others was MS Dhoni. They wanted to become a singer and an athlete respectively. I got truly inspired and created their Vision boards with many beautiful images. My kids were so happy that they went to each and every kid and started showing proudly their boards. I told them they need to see it each morning and strive to be that.
The sweet moment came when we were having, debrief and my kids rushed towards me and said Thank you. They way they said it and emotions can't be described with words... 😇
This was my story and a small glimpse of the vision boards that they created... 🌠🌠

name: Jay's Progress
story:
This is an experience very close to my heart!✨On my very first day, I was assigned to teach a child, Jay. But to my surprise, Jay didn't even want to look at me. He wouldn't speak to me or anyone else. It completely broke my spirit. I remember thinking, "If he won't even respond to me, how will I find the motivation to teach him?"
That's when another child told me something that changed everything - Jay was from Tamil Nadu. In that moment, I decided I would do something different. I spent the next week learning a bit of Tamil, enough to connect with him. When I saw him again, I greeted him in his mother tongue.
And guess what? It worked! Slowly but surely, Jay began to open up. Week after week, I tried this approach . He went from ignoring me to being one of the first kids to run up and greet me at the center.
By the third or fourth week, something truly unforgettable happened. One day, another child was crying, and Jay turned to me and said, "Akka, he is crying. It's wrong. You shouldn't cry all the time, right? " That moment was so precious—it felt like a breakthrough. I was so proud of him, not just for his progress in opening up, but for showing empathy and kindness toward others.
This experience taught me something invaluable: these children aren’t uninterested or ignorant. They’re just waiting for someone to be patient, someone who doesn’t give up on them even when it’s hard.
We have the power to make a difference—not through extraordinary measures, but through simple acts of care, consistency, and understanding. Every child has potential; they just need someone who believes in them enough to bring it out.
Patience and effort could be the key to unlocking a child’s world. Let’s keep showing up for them, even on the days it feels like nothing is working. The smallest steps can lead to the most remarkable journeys!❤️

name: Kailash, a New Beginning
story: I've been teaching a very hyperactive student for over three months now, and from day one, he's been full of energy, but did not want to sit still or focus. After a few weeks, while revisiting a previous lesson, he seemed engaged at first but suddenly ran to the washroom and hid for 10 minutes. When he returned, he crawled under the bed and refused to talk, no matter how much I tried. Even my leaders’ attempts—games, coloring, and outdoor activities—didn’t help. He just wanted to be left alone. It was disheartening, I did not know what to do. The next class, I came prepared with interactive activities—alphabet cards, dictation games, and rewards. At first, he resisted, even hitting his head on the bed when I called him. But when I showed him the fun materials, he finally agreed to sit with me. By the end of the class, he was fully engaged, eager to learn, and at the end of the session he came to me and asked 'Akka, are you coming to teach me next week?'.That moment felt like a huge win and kept motivating me to the next sessions.

name: Ali's Persistence
story: One of my students had trouble reading a few letters in the starting of the course but by the end now he scored 10/10 on all letters and sounds which makes me so proud of him.
